column1: # Forbric kernel -- Minecraft-line rename table for 1.21.1
# The runtime source set (src/runtime/java) is written in the 26.2 namespace. A second Minecraft line gets
# the table below applied at build time, because every entry here is a MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE name: it exists on
# one line and does not exist on the other. Re-measure, do not trust this sentence:
#     python build/x11/probe.py net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation net.minecraft.resources.Identifier
#     net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation    1.21.1=PRESENT  26.2=absent
#     net.minecraft.resources.Identifier          1.21.1=absent   26.2=PRESENT
# So no single spelling compiles on both lines, and a blanket rename in the sources is not available. Each
# entry below was checked in BOTH directions against the staged merged bases
# (forbric-kernel/.dev/staged-1211/run/merged-base/ for 1.21.1, forbric-kernel/run/merged-base/ for 26.2)
# and, where a member is involved, against the method signature with `javap`.
# Format: <26.2 name> TAB <1.21.1 name>   ('#' starts a comment; blank lines ignored)
# Rules are applied longest-first and whole-token only ((?<![A-Za-z0-9_$]) ... (?![A-Za-z0-9_$])), so
# `Identifier` never reaches inside `KernelIdentifier` and a fully-qualified rule always wins over its own
# simple name. The build FAILS if a rule matches nothing, so a table entry that has gone stale is an error
# rather than a silent no-op.
# Mojang renamed ResourceLocation -> Identifier in 26.x. Same class, same members: parse, tryParse,
# tryBuild, fromNamespaceAndPath, withDefaultNamespace, getNamespace, getPath all exist on both sides
# (javap, 1.21.1 ResourceLocation / 26.2 Identifier).
net.minecraft.resources.Identifier
Identifier
# A member rename, not a class rename. 26.2 ResourceKey has `Identifier identifier()` and no `location()`;
# 1.21.1 ResourceKey has `ResourceLocation location()` and no `identifier()` (javap both). 17 call sites,
# all on a ResourceKey. TagKey#location() already has this name on BOTH lines, so it is left alone -- the
# rule rewrites `identifier()`, which TagKey never had.
identifier()
# Renamed to MobSpawnType. Verified through the method that consumes it: 1.21.1
# Mob#finalizeSpawn(ServerLevelAccessor, DifficultyInstance, MobSpawnType, SpawnGroupData), and
# MobSpawnType.SPAWNER / NATURAL / MOB_SUMMONED / TRIGGERED / TRIAL_SPAWNER all exist.
net.minecraft.world.entity.EntitySpawnReason
EntitySpawnReason

# EntityType, whose ZOMBIE / DROWNED / ZOMBIE_VILLAGER / SKELETON / SPIDER are public static finals. A
# whole-token rule, so `EntityType` written already -- which the sources never do -- would be untouched.
net.minecraft.world.entity.EntityTypes
EntityTypes

# the paddle constants and is the common base of the boat family.
net.minecraft.world.entity.vehicle.boat.AbstractBoat
AbstractBoat

# (ParticleEngine); 1.21.1 has the two roles on ParticleEngine, which is the class that implements
# PreparableReloadListener and owns the `providers` map the kernel reads on both lines. Role-based mapping,
# which is why it is written down: it is the one entry here that is not a literal rename.
# THE FULLY-QUALIFIED ROW IS RETIRED IN PLACE (overlay-steals-rules, third occurrence). Its only site was the
# `import net.minecraft.client.particle.ParticleResources;` in KernelForgeClientInit, and that file is now an
# overlay (it needs the 1.21.1 listeners field, see the tail) -- overlays are written verbatim, so the row
# matched nothing and normalizeRuntimeJava would fail with "1 rule(s) matched nothing". Caught by
# overlay-rules.py BEFORE the build, not by the build. The BARE row below is kept because it still has a site
# (the {@code ParticleResources} mention in KernelParticleProviders' javadoc, which the normaliser rewrites like
# any other text) -- so the ported line's documentation keeps this line's class name.
# net.minecraft.client.particle.ParticleResources
ParticleResources
# AXIS 2 -- Forge/NeoForge 26.x API, measured against 1.21.1
# EventBus 7 gives every event class its own static typed bus (`X.BUS`). EventBus 6.2.33 has no such field
# anywhere; the same event is posted on the one game bus, whose declaration was read out of the staged 1.21.1
# forge-runtime.jar:
#     public static final net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api.IEventBus EVENT_BUS;
#                                         (net.minecraftforge.common.MinecraftForge)
# Each rule below is therefore a claim that THIS event belongs on the game bus on 1.21.1 -- not "BUS lives
# somewhere else". The claim was measured per event, two ways, before the rule was written:
#   (a) the event does not implement `net.minecraftforge.fml.event.IModBusEvent` on 1.21.1 (javap), and
#   (b) where the Forge hook is reachable, its bytecode posts it with
#       `getstatic net/minecraftforge/common/MinecraftForge.EVENT_BUS` (javap -c, method-level):
#         ForgeEventFactory        LivingHealEvent, PermissionsChangedEvent, BlockEvent$EntityPlaceEvent,
#                                  EntityEvent$EnteringSection, MobSpawnEvent$FinalizeSpawn
#         ForgeHooks               CriticalHitEvent, AnvilUpdateEvent, BlockEvent$BreakEvent,
#                                  LivingEvent$LivingVisibilityEvent
#         ServerLifecycleHooks     ServerAboutToStartEvent
#         ClientCommandHandler     RegisterClientCommandsEvent
#         ForgeHooksClient         ScreenEvent$Render$Pre/Post, ViewportEvent$RenderFog,
#                                  ViewportEvent$ComputeFogColor
#         ForgeEventFactoryClient  ScreenEvent$MouseButtonPressed$Pre, MouseButtonReleased$Pre
# Both spellings appear where the sources use both, because the substitution is textual: a rule written for
# the short form would otherwise fire inside the fully qualified one. Longest-first ordering is what keeps
# that honest, and a rule that matches nothing fails the build.
net.minecraftforge.event.entity.player.PlayerInteractEvent.EntityInteractSpecific.BUS

# ContainerStorage (fabric-transfer-api-v1 8.0.11, the 26.2 line) -> InventoryStorage (0.116.17, 1.21.1).
# Same package net.fabricmc.fabric.api.transfer.v1.item, same shape: both SlottedStorage<ItemVariant>, both
# of(Container, Direction) + getSlots() + getSlotCount() + getSlot(int). MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE, checked by
# listing both jars rather than by reading a changelog: 26.2's module contains ContainerStorage.class and no
# InventoryStorage.class; 1.21.1's contains InventoryStorage.class and no ContainerStorage.class.
# THIS ENTRY WAS DELIBERATELY ABSENT FOR TWO ROUNDS, and it is a rule only now that its precondition holds.
# While the 1.21.1 fabric-api modules were still intermediary-remapped, InventoryStorage.of took
# (net.minecraft.class_1263, net.minecraft.class_2350), so substituting the name moved three "cannot find
# symbol ContainerStorage" into three "incompatible types: Container cannot be converted to class_1263" --
# same total, different bucket, with the real gap hidden behind a rename that looks like a fix.
# remapTransferApis now rewrites those modules out of intermediary, and javap on the REMAPPED 1.21.1 module
# shows what the call sites actually need:
#     public static net.fabricmc.fabric.api.transfer.v1.item.InventoryStorage
#         of(net.minecraft.world.Container, net.minecraft.core.Direction);
# Both KernelFabricHopperStorage call sites pass a Mojmap Container (HopperBlockEntity / Hopper) and a Mojmap
# Direction, so they satisfy that signature. Measured effect of this one line: 3 errors, see the axis-3 note.
ContainerStorage
# --- AXIS 2, two more renames: a type that CHANGED PACKAGE between the lines ---------------------------
# Both are the same shape as ResourceLocation <-> Identifier -- MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE, one spelling per line --
# and both were found by an exhaustive sweep (build/x11/rename-sweep.py) rather than by eye: for every name
# javac reported absent, every class on the 1.21.1 measurement classpath (39 jars) was listed when it shares
# ALL of that name's words. Of the 55 absent names on axes 1-3, only FOUR have any such candidate at all, and
# these are two of the four.
# WHY A FULLY-QUALIFIED RULE AND NOT A SIMPLE-NAME ONE: the simple name does not change, so the two rules
# below rewrite the IMPORT and let every bare use resolve through it. A bare `Result` rule would fire inside
# its own target (…Event.Result) and inside net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult; a bare `TriState` rule
# would fire inside net.fabricmc.fabric.api.util.TriState. Longest-first ordering cannot save either,
# because the substitution is textual and the simple name survives it.
# 1. net.minecraftforge.common.util.Result -> net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api.Event.Result
#    26.2 pulled MinecraftForge's decision enum OUT of Event: `net.minecraftforge.common.util.Result`
#    (javap, 26.2: ALLOW/DEFAULT/DENY, isAllowed/isDefault/isDenied). 1.21.1 still has it nested, with the
#    same three constants and the same three predicates:
#        public final class net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api.Event$Result extends Enum
#            DENY, DEFAULT, ALLOW; isDefault(); isDenied(); isAllowed();            (javap, 1.21.1)
#    Verified through the method that consumes it, on both lines:
#        26.2    PlayerInteractEvent$RightClickBlock.getUseBlock() : net.minecraftforge.common.util.Result
#        1.21.1  PlayerInteractEvent$RightClickBlock.getUseBlock() : net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api.Event$Result
#    THE `$` FORM OF THIS TARGET DOES NOT COMPILE, and that is measured, not assumed: `import
#    net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api.Event$Result;` fails with "cannot find symbol: class Event$Result,
#    location: package net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api". The CANONICAL nested spelling is the one that works
#    (`import net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api.Event.Result;` + bare `Result.DENY`); it was compiled by hand
#    against the 1.21.1 classpath before this line was written.
# 2. net.minecraft.util.TriState -> net.neoforged.neoforge.common.util.TriState
#    26.2 adopted NeoForge's tri-state into vanilla: net.minecraft.util.TriState exists on 26.2 and is
#    ABSENT from every one of the 39 1.21.1 jars; net.neoforged.neoforge.common.util.TriState exists on
#    1.21.1 (javap: TRUE/DEFAULT/FALSE, isTrue/isDefault/isFalse) and is ABSENT from 26.2's
#    neoforge-runtime.jar. Verified through the consumer method, on both lines:
#        26.2    (NeoForge) PlayerInteractEvent$RightClickBlock.getUseBlock() : net.minecraft.util.TriState
#        1.21.1  (NeoForge) PlayerInteractEvent$RightClickBlock.getUseBlock() : net.neoforged.neoforge.
#                                                                            common.util.TriState
#    Both files that touch these two types use them only as the bridge's value type (KernelGameBlockEvents:
#    TriState <-> Result; KernelGameWorldEvents: Result), and the enum constants used are the same three, so
#    the substitution carries every call site. THIS IS NOT VERIFIED BEYOND COMPILATION: nothing has executed
#    either bridge on 1.21.1.
net.minecraftforge.common.util.Result
# --- AXIS 2, two more renames found by asking the MEMBERS, not the class names ------------------------
# The word-overlap sweep cannot see either of these: it compares CLASS simple names, and both of these are
# member renames inside a class that has the same name on both lines. They were found by listing the members
# of the class javac had already resolved and diffing the two listings, which is the only method that finds
# a rename whose owner did not move.
# 1. ForgeHooks.ingredientBaseCodec(Codec<Ingredient>) -> ForgeHooks.enhanceIngredientCodec(Codec<Ingredient>)
#    Same class, same parameter type, same return type, same body -- three private lambdas each, doing the
#    same three things (unwrap Either, re-encode, report a failure) -- and MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE:
#        26.2    ingredientBaseCodec(Codec<Ingredient>) : Codec<Ingredient>      (javap)
#                lambda$ingredientBaseCodec$0/$1/$2
#        1.21.1  enhanceIngredientCodec(Codec<Ingredient>) : Codec<Ingredient>    (javap)
#                lambda$enhanceIngredientCodec$17/$18/$19
#    Neither name exists on the other line (both listings are in the sweep output: 26.2 has no
#    enhanceIngredientCodec, 1.21.1 has no ingredientBaseCodec). One call site, KernelForgeIngredients:72.
ingredientBaseCodec
# 2. net.neoforged.neoforge.client.event.RegisterColorHandlersEvent.BlockTintSources
#        -> net.neoforged.neoforge.client.event.RegisterColorHandlersEvent.Block
#    26.2 renamed this event class inside the NEOFORGE package tree only, and that is visible by comparing the
#    two trees on the SAME line -- it is the CompatLayer-style rename 26.2 applies between them (javap, all
#    four classes):
#        26.2    neoforged...RegisterColorHandlersEvent$BlockTintSources   PRESENT   register(List<BlockTintSource>, Block...)
#        26.2    neoforged...RegisterColorHandlersEvent$Block              ABSENT
#        1.21.1  neoforged...RegisterColorHandlersEvent$BlockTintSources   ABSENT
#        1.21.1  neoforged...RegisterColorHandlersEvent$Block              PRESENT   register(BlockColor, Block...)
#    Both io versions carry getBlockColors(), which is the ONLY member the kernel reads
#    (KernelForgeBlockColors.postBlockTintSources casts the event and asks it for the live BlockColors), so the
#    read path is a plain rename. THE RULE IS NOT THE WHOLE STORY AND IS NOT A LIE EITHER: register(...) takes
#    List<BlockTintSource> on 26.2 and BlockColor on 1.21.1, and BlockTintSource is a 26.x vanilla type that
#    does not exist on 1.21.1 -- so the registration path, if the kernel ever needed it, would be an axis-1
#    restructure. It never calls register.
#    It also stays honest about where the event comes from: ForgeBlockTintInjector redirects BlockColors's own
#    post call, so the object cast here is whatever THAT body constructed -- and 1.21.1's body constructs
#    RegisterColorHandlersEvent.Block (javap of BlockColors.createDefault's call). The cast is right on both lines.
RegisterColorHandlersEvent.BlockTintSources
# --- Minecraft#getTimer, renamed to getDeltaTracker in 26.2 -----------------------------------------------
# A member rename with the SAME return type on both lines: 26.2 has `public DeltaTracker getDeltaTracker()`
# and NO getTimer(); 1.21.1 has `public DeltaTracker getTimer()` and NO getDeltaTracker() (javap -p both).
# Both return their line's own net.minecraft.client.DeltaTracker, and both of those interfaces declare
# getRealtimeDeltaTicks(), which is the only member the kernel calls:
#     KernelGameClientEvents:150   Minecraft.getInstance().getDeltaTracker().getRealtimeDeltaTicks()
# One call site, so a rule is the whole fix.
getDeltaTracker
# Another member rename on a class BOTH lines have. It is written qualified on purpose, and the reason is the
# trap in it -- javap -p net.minecraft.core.Registry:
#     26.2    T getValue(ResourceKey<T>)   T getValue(Identifier)   Optional<Holder$Reference<T>> get(Identifier)
#     1.21.1  T get(ResourceKey)           T get(ResourceLocation)  Optional<Holder$Reference<T>> getHolder(...)
# 26.2 shifted BOTH names down one: the old get became getValue, and the old getHolder became get. So a bare
# `getValue -> get` row is NOT safe: `getValue` occurs 49 times in src/runtime/java and nearly all of them are
# Map.Entry#getValue() (KernelForgeOptions, KernelForgeSpawnPlacements, KernelCreativeSearch's
# `tab.getValue()`, IdentityValueBiMap's own override). A whole-token rule on the bare name would rewrite every
# one of those into a get() that Map.Entry does not have. Written qualified, the receiver expression is
# untouched and only the member name changes -- a name, not an expression rewrite. Qualification is the
# established form here: the `.BUS` rows above do the same thing.
#     KernelParticleProviders:150   BuiltInRegistries.PARTICLE_TYPE.getValue(e.getKey())
BuiltInRegistries.PARTICLE_TYPE.getValue

# SITES THAT LOOK EXACTLY LIKE THE RULES ABOVE AND MUST NOT GET ONE. Each would compile and be wrong:
#   SpawnPlacementRegisterEvent.BUS          implements net.minecraftforge.fml.event.IModBusEvent
#   RegisterClientReloadListenersEvent.BUS   implements net.minecraftforge.fml.event.IModBusEvent   (javap)
#       Both fire on the MOD event bus. In 6.2.33 that bus has NO name: it is reached through
#       FMLJavaModLoadingContext.get().getModEventBus(), an expression, and this file maps names. Pointing
#       them at EVENT_BUS would compile and silently deliver the event to nobody -- the exact failure mode
#       this tail exists to prevent.
#   EntityEvent.EnteringSection.BUS          called as `.BUS.hasListeners()`.
#   LivingEvent.LivingVisibilityEvent.BUS    Same. net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api.IEventBus in 6.2.33 has no
#       hasListeners() at all (javap: register, addListener x4, addGenericListener x4, unregister, post x2,
#       fire x2, shutdown, start). Rewriting the receiver would trade "cannot find symbol BUS" for "cannot
#       find symbol hasListeners" -- one error for another, which is not a fix and would move the error out of
#       this axis's count for no reason.
#   AttachCapabilitiesEvent.{Levels,Entities,BlockEntities}.BUS
#       Those three inner classes do not exist on 1.21.1. This is the 26.x capability-provider split already
#       recorded in docs/1.21.1-port.md stage 3 (1.21.1 CapabilityProvider has 2 inner classes, 26.2 has 7).
# --- measured absent, with no same-simple-name counterpart anywhere in 1.21.1 -----------------------
# HOW THIS LIST WAS MADE, AND HOW IT WAS RE-CHECKED TWICE. The first pass indexed the three staged 1.21.1 jars
# (12,505 classes) and searched by simple name. That misses exactly the rename worth finding -- the one where the
# words survive and the nesting or noun does not (BreakBlockEvent -> BlockEvent$BreakEvent) -- and it also produced
# two WRONG entries that are corrected below. The second pass indexed the whole MEASUREMENT CLASS PATH (39 jars,
# build/x11/index-nested.json, nested classes included) and, for every name javac reported absent, listed every
# class there whose own CamelCase words contain ALL of that name's words (build/x11/rename-sweep.py).
# THIS ROUND ADDED A THIRD METHOD, because the second one cannot see a member rename: it compares CLASS simple
# names, and both renames it missed live inside a class that has the SAME name on both lines. So for every error
# javac reported as "cannot find symbol: method" or "method ... cannot be applied to given types", the class
# javac had ALREADY RESOLVED was listed with `javap -p` on both carriers and the two member listings were
# diffed. That is what found ingredientBaseCodec -> enhanceIngredientCodec and
# BlockTintSources -> Block; both are rules now, above.
# MEASURED AFTER THIS ROUND: 55 distinct absent names on the final transcript, 9 with at least one word-overlap
# candidate, and NONE of those 9 is the same concept. The thirteen that share words and nothing else:
# EnergyHandler vs EnergyStorage / IEnergyStorage (different method sets), ResourceHandler vs fabric's
# ResourceAmount, Resource vs ResourceKey, TransactionContext vs fabric's own class of that name,
# TransformingClassLoader/ClassTransformer vs cpw.mods.modlauncher's (a different platform, see below),
# FluidModel vs DynamicFluidContainerModel, WeightedList/Weighted vs WeightedRandomList (axis 1),
# Entities/Levels vs ChunkEntities/EnchantWithLevelsFunction (the AttachCapabilitiesEvent inners),
# ClassProcessor vs Mixin's IClassProcessor. The compile is the oracle for absence: javac read all 39 jars and
# did not find the name.
# EVERY REMAINING AXIS-2 NAME, ADJUDICATED. Each line says what 26.2 has, what 1.21.1 has (javap, both carriers,
# 1.21.1 = the 39-jar measurement class path), and whether it is a RENAME (a rule) or a RESTRUCTURE (code), and
# whether this round did it. The count in brackets is that name's share of the 95 axis-2 errors left.
#   net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api.bus.BusGroup    [8]  RESTRUCTURE, not done.
#       EventBus 7 only. `BusGroup.create(...)` + `.startup()` (KernelForgeContainers, KernelForgeSetup,
#       KernelForgeRegistries) is 7's group lifecycle; 1.21.1 has IEventBus and no BusGroup. Its counterpart is
#       POSITIVE, not absent: net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api.BusBuilder exists on 1.21.1 and is how a standalone
#       bus is built there, so this is an expression rewrite (BusBuilder.builder().build()), not a name -- and
#       the type that receives it is passed into FMLModContainer's eventBusGroup field, which is typed BusGroup
#       on 26.2. Refused for that reason, not for absence. The design question (does the 1.21.1 line still need
#       a per-mod group at all, or one mod bus) is not answered by a name.
#   net.neoforged.neoforgespi.transformation.*      [22]  RESTRUCTURE, not done.
#   net.neoforged.fml.classloading.transformation.*
#       Absent from both 1.21.1 carriers. 1.21.1 transforms through modlauncher, and modlauncher's classes ARE on
#       the measurement class path -- so this is the closest a refusal gets to a rename, and it is still not one.
#       WHERE those classes live is part of the evidence: cpw.mods.modlauncher.TransformingClassLoader is in
#       forge-runtime.jar on BOTH lines (not in neoforge-runtime.jar on either), so the platform is present twice
#       over and it is the NEOFORGE-side API the kernel uses that is 26.2-only. A substitution would move the name
#       and leave the shape (next paragraph).
#       KernelFmlTransformerView builds a VIEW: it allocates a TransformingClassLoader, writes a ClassTransformer
#       into its `classTransformer` field, a ClassProcessorSet into that transformer's `processors`, and the
#       kernel's IMixinTransformer into FMLMixinClassProcessor's `transformer`, so a NeoForge mod (LibJF) that
#       casts the context loader and walks that chain reaches the weaver that weaves. Measured on both sides:
#           26.2    transforming.TransformingClassLoader{ private final ClassTransformer classTransformer; }
#                   transforming.ClassTransformer{ Processors processors; }
#                   neoforgespi.transformation.ClassProcessorSet{ SequencedMap processors; }
#                   loading.mixin.FMLMixinClassProcessor{ IMixinTransformer transformer; }
#           1.21.1  cpw.mods.modlauncher.TransformingClassLoader
#                       { private final cpw.mods.modlauncher.ClassTransformer classTransformer; }   <- SAME field name
#                   cpw.mods.modlauncher.ClassTransformer
#                       { TransformStore transformers; LaunchPluginHandler pluginHandler;
#                         TransformingClassLoader transformingClassLoader; TransformerAuditTrail auditTrail; }
